schemeHints.jwtBearer: Signs a JWT with every request. HS* use the shared secret; RS* and ES* a PEM private key. iat is added if the payload has none. Values may use environment variables.
schemeHints.digest: The request goes out, the server answers 401 with its terms, and the request goes again with the answer (MD5, SHA-256, -sess, qop auth and auth-int).
schemeHints.oauth1: Signs each request (RFC 5849): method, URL, query and form body. Leave the token empty for two-legged OAuth.
schemeHints.hawk: Signs method, path, host and port with a timestamp and nonce; tick the body hash if the server verifies payloads.
schemeHints.aws: AWS Signature Version 4. Leave the service empty to read it from an *.amazonaws.com host; S3 also gets the payload hash header.
schemeHints.ntlm: NTLMv2 handshake on one connection, from this server or from the agent. DOMAIN\user in the username works too.
schemeHints.akamai: EG1-HMAC-SHA256, with the three credentials of your .edgerc section. The body of POST requests is hashed up to the maximum.
schemeHints.asap: A short-lived JWT signed with your service's private key, sent as a Bearer token. A fresh jti on every request.

mfa.scan: Scan this with an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, 1Password…), then enter the code it shows.
mfa.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
mfa.manual: Or type this key in by hand:
mfa.codeOrRecovery: Code from the app, or a recovery code
mfa.requiredNote: Your organization requires it, so it cannot be turned off.

recoveryCodes.title: Save your recovery codes
recoveryCodes.body: Each one signs you in once if you lose your phone. This is the only time they are shown.

policy.label: Require it of every member
policy.hint: Members without it are asked to set it up before they can do anything else. API keys are not affected.
policy.needsOwn: Turn it on for yourself first.

required.title: Set up two-factor authentication
required.body: Your organization requires a code from an authenticator app at every sign-in. Set it up to continue.

challenge.label: Code from your authenticator app
challenge.hint: Lost your phone? Enter one of your recovery codes instead.

projectAccess.title: Who can reach {{name}}
projectAccess.description: Restricted, the project and its tests are visible only to owners and the people listed here. A role here never gives more than the person’s role in the organization.
projectAccess.onlyOwners: Nobody is listed: only owners can reach it.

publishing.runsWorkingCopy: Not published: plans run the latest save.
publishing.runsNothing: Not published: plans skip this test until a reviewed version is published.
publishing.unpublishedChanges: Version {{n}} has changes that are not published yet.

reviews.title: Test reviews
reviews.description: A saved test is a working copy. Plans run the published version. Approving a review here publishes that version.
reviews.policyHint: Publishing then needs another member’s approval, and plans skip tests that have never been published. Rolling back to a version that was live before stays possible.
reviews.error: The reviews could not be loaded.
reviews.reasonRequired: Say what needs to change before rejecting.
reviews.notYours: Someone other than its author has to decide on this change.

testHistory.rollbackHint: Plans run this version again. It was live before.
testHistory.title: History of "{{name}}"
testHistory.description: Every save is here, newest first. Restoring one adds it to the top as a new version — nothing between is removed, and today’s work stays recoverable.
testHistory.empty: Nothing yet. The next save is version 1.
testHistory.unversioned_one: {{count}} earlier run of this test did not record which version it used.
testHistory.unversioned_other: {{count}} earlier runs of this test did not record which version they used.

runners.error: The runners could not be loaded.
runners.none: No runner is taking work: every new run will wait in the queue. Start a worker (npm run dev:worker, or the worker service).
runners.drainHint: Draining lets a runner finish what it is running and take nothing new. When its jobs reach zero it can be stopped safely.
runners.readOnly: Runners serve every organization on this installation, so draining one is for its administrators.

suites.title: Suites
suites.pageDescription: Lists of tests kept once and shared by the plans that include them.
suites.error: The suites could not be loaded.
suites.empty: No suites yet. A suite keeps a list of tests once, for every plan that needs it.

kindHint.static: These tests, in the order you pick them.
kindHint.dynamic: Every test carrying all of the chosen tags, worked out when a run is created.

fields.name: Name
fields.tags: Tags (a test must carry all of them)

dialog.description: A suite is a list of tests kept once and included by as many plans as need it.

suites.noTags: No tags yet: add them from the test library.
suites.hiddenTest: A test in a project you cannot see
suites.loadFailed: The suite could not be loaded
suites.deleteInPlans: {{count}} plans include it; they will stop running its tests. Runs already made keep what they ran.

planSuites.title: Suites in "{{name}}"
planSuites.description: They run after the plan's own tests, in the order you tick them. A test in more than one runs once.

flakyTests.title: Tests that disagree with themselves
flakyTests.description: Over the last {{days}} days, the tests whose verdict changed from one run to the next with nothing to explain it. A test that broke and was fixed is not here, and neither is one whose verdict changed because somebody edited it.
flakyTests.empty: No test changed its mind in this window — out of {{count}} results examined.
flakyTests.editedTitle: Edited during this window (versions {{versions}}). Only the unexplained changes of verdict are counted.

quarantine.title: Quarantine "{{name}}"
quarantine.explain: It keeps running and its results are kept, so you can see when it is fixed. Its failures stop failing runs, stopping plans, filing issues and breaking pipelines until somebody releases it.
quarantine.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. times out waiting for the payment iframe about one night in three
quarantine.listDescription: They still run. Their failures are recorded but do not fail runs or pipelines. Release a test once it has been passing again.
quarantine.error: The quarantined tests could not be loaded.
quarantine.ready: Passed its last {{count}} runs: ready to release
quarantine.released: "{{name}}" is back: its failures count again
quarantine.badgeTitle: This test was in quarantine: a failure of it does not fail the run.

accessibility.title: Accessibility check
accessibility.summary: {{violations}} rules broken, {{passes}} passed, {{incomplete}} need a person to check · fails at {{threshold}} or worse
accessibility.clean: No rule was broken on this page.

evidence.networkHelp: The report lists the failed and slowest requests of every recorded test, kept file or not. The HAR opens in any browser’s DevTools; it never holds bodies, cookies, tokens or passwords.
evidence.label: Keep a recording of the run
evidence.help: A report holds a picture per step and the message it died with. A video and a Playwright trace answer what that cannot — a slow request, a dialog that came and went, a page that moved under the click. Both cost disk on every run.

runOn.label: Run on
runOn.help: Where the tests run from. A pool of local agents opens pages and sends API requests from inside its own network.

editTestPlanSettings.title: Run settings
editTestPlanSettings.description: What "{{name}}" does on its next run.

validation.webhookUrlInvalid: The notification URL must start with http:// or https://.
validation.parallelInvalid: Run at most must be a whole number between 1 and 16.
validation.localesInvalid: Not a language code: {{codes}}. Use codes such as it, it-IT or en-US.
validation.shardsInvalid: Workers must be a whole number between 1 and 8.

browsers.label: Browsers
browsers.help: Every test in this plan runs once per browser listed here. With none listed, a run uses the browser from your own settings.

parallel.label: Run at most (tests at once)
parallel.help: Each one is a real browser session, so this is a statement about the runner. 1 runs the plan one test at a time, browser by browser. A plan whose API tests capture values for later requests keeps those in order within each browser.

visualTesting.label: Visual testing
visualTesting.help: Compare each step against its stored baseline. The first run after turning this on records the baselines.

issues.noTracker: Nowhere — failures stay in the report
issues.autoLabel: Open an issue when a test fails
issues.autoHelp: One issue per failing test and browser. The same failure tomorrow night is added to it as a comment, not opened again.

webhook.label: Send notifications to (webhook URL)
webhook.help: A Slack or Microsoft Teams incoming webhook, or any URL that accepts a POST. Without one, nothing is sent.

locales.label: Languages
locales.help: Each test runs once per language on every browser, with the browser set to that language; steps read it as {{token}}. Empty runs in the browser’s own language.

testManagement.label: Publish results to
testManagement.none: Nowhere — results stay in the report
testManagement.help: Every finished run becomes a TestRail run, an Xray Test Execution or a Zephyr test cycle, with each test’s result under its case. Tests with no case are left out.

shards.label: Workers sharing a run
shards.help: Splits one run across up to this many runners, each running the number above at once. Tests are handed out one at a time to whichever runner is free, and the report is one run as usual. 1 keeps the run on one runner.

network.title: Network
network.download: Download the HAR (opens in any browser’s DevTools)

html.label: HTML report
html.hint: One file that opens anywhere, screenshots included

pdf.label: PDF
pdf.hint: To attach to a ticket or file for an audit

allure.label: Allure results (.zip)
allure.hint: For allure generate or an Allure server

junit.label: JUnit XML
junit.hint: For a CI system’s test report

issueTrackers.allFieldsRequired: Name, URL, project and token are all needed.
issueTrackers.emailRequired: Jira needs the email address the API token belongs to.
issueTrackers.title: Issue trackers
issueTrackers.description: Where a failing test becomes somebody’s ticket. A plan can then file its failures automatically, and the same failure the next night becomes a comment rather than a second issue.
issueTrackers.name: Name
issueTrackers.tokenHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again. To change it, type a new one.
issueTrackers.empty: No tracker yet. Until there is one, failures stay in the report.

restored.title: Restored
restored.description: The test is back to version {{from}}, saved as version {{to}}.
restored.unchanged: The test already was that version, so nothing changed.

testLibrary.title: Test Library
testLibrary.description: Every saved test, what it is for, and what it used to be.
testLibrary.empty: No tests yet. Record or describe one in the builder and save it.

authorSteps.title: Describe the test
authorSteps.description: One instruction per line, in the words the ticket used. Every line is shown as the step it became before anything is inserted — a sentence read the wrong way would otherwise become a test that passes for the wrong reason.
authorSteps.placeholder:
Go to https://example.com/login
Type "admin" into the Username field
Click the Sign in button
Check that the dashboard is visible
authorSteps.projectLabel: Project whose elements may be named (optional)
authorSteps.noProject: Only what is detected on this page
authorSteps.projectHint: A step that names a kept element reads its selector from the repository, so a later repair reaches this test too.
authorSteps.noModel: No AI key is configured, so only the phrasings this understands on its own were read.

keepElement.projectRequired: Choose the project this element belongs to.
keepElement.nameRequired: Give the element a name — it is how it will be recognised.
keepElement.title: Keep this element
keepElement.description: The project owns this element from now on: every test that uses it reads one selector, and a repair reaches all of them at once.

saveStepGroup.nameRequired: Give the group a name — it is how tests will call it.
saveStepGroup.title: Save as step group
saveStepGroup.description_one: This step becomes a group. A test that calls it runs whatever the group holds at the time it runs, so editing the group later changes every test that calls it.
saveStepGroup.description_other: These {{count}} steps become a group. A test that calls it runs whatever the group holds at the time it runs, so editing the group later changes every test that calls it.

tags.none: No tags yet. The first word you type becomes one.

sso.title: Single sign-on
sso.description: Members sign in with your identity provider (OpenID Connect or SAML 2.0: Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace, ADFS, Keycloak…). The first time someone from your domains signs in, their account is created.
sso.callbackUrl: Redirect URI to register with your provider
sso.secretKept: Stored. Leave empty to keep it.
sso.enabledHint: Off keeps the settings and signs nobody in through the provider.
sso.requiredHint: Members other than owners can no longer sign in with a password, and their password sessions end. Owners keep theirs, to get back in if the provider fails. API keys are not affected.
sso.removalNote: Your provider decides who gets in: someone removed here comes back with a new account at their next sign-in. End their access at the provider — with SCIM provisioning, that deactivates them here at once — or map groups and refuse whoever is in none.
sso.requiredAtLogin: Your organization signs in with single sign-on. Use "Sign in with SSO" below.

errors.unknown_domain: No organization here signs in that address with single sign-on. Check it, or sign in with your password.
errors.provider_unreachable: Your organization's identity provider could not be reached. Try again, or ask an owner to check the single sign-on settings.
errors.expired: The sign-in took too long, or was started in another window. Try again.
errors.provider_error: Your identity provider did not complete the sign-in. Try again; if it keeps happening, an owner will find the reason in the server log.
errors.no_email: Your identity provider did not send your e-mail address. An owner has to add the email claim to the application there.
errors.email_unverified: Your identity provider says your e-mail address is not verified.
errors.domain_not_allowed: Your e-mail address is not in a domain your organization signs in.
errors.account_elsewhere: An account with your address belongs to another organization on this installation.
errors.account_linked: Your address is already linked to another identity at your provider. Ask an owner of your organization.
errors.browser_mismatch: This sign-in was started in another browser. Start it again here.
errors.no_group: Your account at the identity provider is in none of the groups this organization lets in. Ask your administrator.

saml.spHint: Give your identity provider these values, or the metadata URL, which carries them all.
saml.metadataUrl: Service provider metadata URL (available once saved)
saml.pasteMetadata: Your provider's metadata (optional: fills the three fields below)
saml.metadataRead: Filled from the metadata. Check the values, then save.
saml.certExpired: Expired on {{date}}: sign-ins are refused until you paste the new certificate.
saml.idpInitiatedCaution: Off by default. Unsolicited sign-in can sign this browser into another account without a login request from WebFlowMaster. Enable only when you trust your provider’s launch flow. Signatures, audience, time limits, domain checks and replay protection still apply.
saml.encryptedHint: Requires a matching service provider certificate and private key. Configure your provider to encrypt assertions with this public certificate.
saml.sloHint: Use the provider’s HTTPS HTTP-Redirect logout endpoint. Single logout requires the matching service provider certificate and private key below.
saml.spCertificateHint: Public RSA X.509 certificate for signing logout messages and decrypting assertions. The certificate must match the private key.
saml.spPrivateKeyHint: Paste the RSA PEM private key. It is stored encrypted and never returned. Leave this field blank to retain a stored key.
saml.removeSpKey: Remove the stored service provider key and certificate
saml.removeSpKeyHint: Turn off required encryption and clear the provider logout URL before removing the key.

domainsProof.title: Proof of the domains
domainsProof.required: On this installation a domain signs nobody in until it is proven: publish its TXT record, then press Verify.
domainsProof.advice: Proving a domain is optional here, and shows your provider is really yours: publish its TXT record, then press Verify.

groups.title: Roles from the provider's groups
groups.hint: At every sign-in the role follows the groups the provider sends: the highest role any of them maps to. With no mapping, roles are managed here in Members.
groups.attribute: Claim or attribute with the groups
groups.require: Refuse whoever is in none of these groups
groups.requireHint: Then removing someone from the groups at the provider ends their access here at their next sign-in.

scim.title: Provisioning (SCIM)
scim.description: Your identity provider creates, deactivates and removes accounts here, and pushes its groups, as soon as they change there — not at the next sign-in. Give it the base URL and a token.
scim.tokenShown: Token — copy it now, it is not shown again
scim.replaceHint: Replacing the token ends the old one at once: paste the new one at the provider.

sso.loadFailed: Could not load single sign-on settings.

manualTests.description: The steps a person performs, each with the result to expect. In a plan run it waits for a verdict in the report.
manualTests.name: Name

errors.name: Give the test a name.
errors.duplicate: A test with this name already exists.

manualResults.title: Manual tests
manualResults.description: Perform each test, mark how every step went, and give the verdict. The run’s counts and status follow.
manualResults.notYet: Results can be recorded once the run has finished.
manualResults.notesPlaceholder: What happened, the issue opened, the environment used

failureAnalysis.title: AI failure analysis
failureAnalysis.loading: Reading the steps, the errors and the requests…
failureAnalysis.failed: The analysis could not be made.
failureAnalysis.caveat: It is a probable cause, not a verdict: check it against the steps.
failureAnalysis.appliedVersion: Applied: the test was saved as version {{version}}. The next run uses it once it is published.
failureAnalysis.applyFailed: The selector could not be applied.
failureAnalysis.inGroup: The step is inside a step group: change it in the group.

start.tooltip: Run step by step: stops at breakpoints and where a step fails

correction.group: This step is inside a step group: a correction applies to this run only.
correction.test: A correction is copied into the test; save it to keep it.

corrected.title: Correction copied into the test
corrected.description: Save the test to keep it.

browserGrids.title: Browser grids
browserGrids.description: Browsers the runners do not have — Windows and macOS, branded Chrome and Edge, older versions — borrowed from BrowserStack, LambdaTest or a Playwright server of your own. A plan picks one in its run settings.
browserGrids.name: Name
browserGrids.endpointHint: Where {token} appears, the token goes there; otherwise it is sent as a bearer token. The server must run the same Playwright version as the runners.
browserGrids.keyHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
browserGrids.checking: Opening a browser on the grid…
browserGrids.empty: No grid yet: plans run on the server’s runners or on local agents.
browserGrids.deleted: {{count}} plan(s) that used it run on the server’s runners again.
browserGrids.loadFailed: Could not load the browser grids.
browserGrids.usernameRequired: A username is required for this provider.
browserGrids.endpointRequired: The address of a Playwright server starts with ws:// or wss://.
browserGrids.keyRequired: An access key is required for this provider.
browserGrids.appiumEndpointInvalid: Appium's address starts with http:// or https://, as the agent's machine reaches it.
browserGrids.poolRequired: Name the pool of local agents that reach Appium.
browserGrids.appiumEndpointHint: Appium's address as the agent's machine reaches it. Empty: {{url}}, where Appium listens when started with no options.
browserGrids.agentPoolHint: An agent of this pool, on the machine next to Appium, carries the requests: the server needs no way into that network.

requirements.title: Requirements
requirements.pageDescription: Epics, user stories and requirements, the tests that cover them, and how those tests did the last time they ran.

dialog.description: An epic, a user story or a requirement. Link tests to it to see whether it is covered and passing.

requirements.keyHint: Letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores, like SHOP-142 or REQ_12.

link.title: Tests covering {{key}}
link.hidden: {{count}} more linked tests are in projects you cannot see; they stay linked.

import.title: Import from a tracker
import.description: Epics and stories are read from the tracker and kept up to date by Sync; nothing is written back to it. A story brings its epic along.
import.noTracker: No Jira or Azure DevOps is connected. Add one in Settings → Issue trackers; the same connection is used here.

requirements.loadFailed: The requirement could not be loaded

scope.label: Results from
scope.all: The latest run of each test

requirements.error: The requirements could not be loaded.
requirements.empty: No requirements yet. Import epics and stories from Jira or Azure DevOps, or add one by hand, then link the tests that cover it.
requirements.deleteBody: Its links to tests go with it; the tests and their results stay. What it contains moves to the top level. Nothing changes in the tracker.

testManagement.deleted: {{count}} plan(s) that published to it no longer publish anywhere.
testManagement.addressRequired: The address of the tool is required.
testManagement.title: Test management
testManagement.description: TestRail, Xray or Zephyr Scale. A plan that names one publishes every finished run there — a TestRail run, an Xray Test Execution, a Zephyr test cycle — with each test’s result under its case.
testManagement.name: Name
testManagement.addressDefault: Empty for {{url}}; the EU or US address for data kept there.
testManagement.tokenHint: Stored encrypted and never shown again.
testManagement.suite: Suite id (for a project with several suites)
testManagement.empty: No connection yet: runs are published nowhere.

cases.title: Test cases in {{name}}
cases.description: The case each test is published as. A key in the test’s name, like [{{example}}] Login, is used when nothing is typed here. Tests with neither are not published.
cases.invalid: Not a case key of this tool (like {{example}}): {{keys}}

publications.title: Test management
publications.description: Where this run was published, case by case. Publishing again makes a new run in the tool, with the verdicts as they are now.
publications.counts: {{published}} case(s) published, {{unmapped}} test(s) with no case left out.

generateTests.nameMissing: Every chosen test needs a name.
generateTests.stepsMissing: Every chosen test needs at least one step.
generateTests.title: Tests for {{key}}
generateTests.description: An AI model reads the story and its acceptance criteria and proposes test cases. Correct them, keep the ones you want, and they become manual tests linked to the story.
generateTests.reading: Reading the story and writing test cases… this can take a minute.
generateTests.fromTracker: Written from {{key}} as the tracker has it now
generateTests.name: Name of test {{n}}

mobileTests.fixSteps: Correct the steps marked in red first.
mobileTests.dialogDescription: An Android or iOS app on a real device of a BrowserStack or LambdaTest grid. Name elements by accessibility id (~login), resource id (id=…), text (text=Sign in) or XPath.
mobileTests.name: Name

run.title: Run {{name}}
run.description: {{device}} on the grid you choose. Finding the device and installing the app takes a minute or two.
run.noGrid: No BrowserStack or LambdaTest grid yet: add one in Settings → Browser grids.
run.session: Video and logs on the grid
run.screenshot: The device at the end of the run

mobileTests.loadFailed: Could not load the mobile tests.

mobileTests.pageDescription: Tests of native Android and iOS apps, on real devices of your BrowserStack or LambdaTest grid.
mobileTests.emptyNoGrid: No mobile test yet. They run on a BrowserStack or LambdaTest grid: add one in Settings → Browser grids first.
mobileTests.deleteBody: Its runs go with it. The app stays on the grid.
mobileTests.noPlanGrid: No grid: not runnable in plans
mobileTests.planGridHint: A test plan runs this test once per run, on this grid, whatever browsers the plan covers.
mobileTests.inspectNeeds: The inspector needs a grid, the app and the device.

mobileInspector.title: Inspector
mobileInspector.description: Pick elements on a real device, or record what you do on it: click the screen, then add steps.
mobileInspector.opening: The grid is finding a {{device}} and installing the app — a minute or two.
mobileInspector.noScreenshot: The grid sent no picture of the screen; pick elements from the list.
mobileInspector.pick: Click an element on the screen, or in the list below.
mobileInspector.cost: The device stays yours while this is open and is released when you close it, or after five minutes without use.
mobileInspector.recordHint: Tap or drag on the screen. Next click:
mobileInspector.noText: This element shows no text to check.
mobileInspector.unnamed: Nothing there can be named, so the tap was done but not recorded.
mobileInspector.recordedEmpty: What you do on the screen appears here. Nothing goes into the test until you add it.

mobileInspector.secretHelp: A password written into the test is visible to everyone who can read it: write {{password}} and set it in the environment.
mobileInspector.discardRecorded: Close and lose the {{count}} recorded step(s) not added to the test?

apiPerformance.enable: Check response times over several requests
apiPerformance.help: In a plan, the request is sent again until the count is reached, a few at once, and the test fails when a threshold is exceeded. Captures come from the first request only. This measures an endpoint; it is not a load test.
apiPerformance.thresholds: Fail the test when (leave empty for no limit)
apiPerformance.reportDescription: API tests that sent their request several times and checked the times against thresholds.

testData.title: Test data
testData.pageDescription: Data kept once and reused by every test: values as {{data.<set>.<column>}}, or the rows a UI test runs over.
testData.dialogHint: A name and a table. The first row gives the {{data.…}} values; a UI test can run over every row.
testData.name: Name
testData.empty: No shared data yet. Create a set for the customers, products or cards your tests keep copying.

organizationData.exportDescription: One JSON file with every table of the organization: members, projects, tests, plans, runs and the audit log. Passwords and tokens are left out; secrets stay encrypted. Treat the file as confidential.
organizationData.eraseDescription: Deletes the organization, every member account, all its data and its files (run evidence and visual baselines). It cannot be undone: download an export first if you may need anything.
organizationData.typeName: Type the organization name, {{name}}, to confirm
organizationData.lastWarning: Erase {{name}} and every account in it? This cannot be undone.

cleanup.title: Cleanup
cleanup.description: API calls made after the test, whether it passed or not, to remove the data it created. Values the steps stored, like {{example}}, can be used; a call naming one the run never set is skipped.
cleanup.add: Add a saved API test as cleanup…
cleanup.empty: No cleanup. What the test creates stays in the application.

testFiles.title: Tests as files
testFiles.description: A project's web and API tests as one YAML or JSON file, to keep in a repository beside the application. Importing it back updates the tests of the same name — each gets a new version — and creates the others. Secrets in API tests are written as variables.
testFiles.gherkinExport: Exports web tests only. WebFlowMaster metadata preserves original actions; Cucumber execution requires your own step definitions.
testFiles.gherkinImport: English Feature, Background, Scenario, Scenario Outline, Examples and tags are supported. Prose imports as manual steps. Descriptions, Rule, doc strings, step data tables and Examples tags are rejected. WFM metadata restores exported web actions.

impactMap.title: Impact map
impactMap.description: Which files affect which tests. Map a file pattern to a tag: a run started with the files a commit changed (wfm run --changed-since) runs the tests carrying the tags those files map to, the tests the map does not cover, and those that failed last time. A changed file no rule matches runs every test.
impactMap.empty: No rules: every run runs every test.
impactMap.filesPlaceholder: One changed file per line, as git diff --name-only lists them

pagePerformance.title: Page speed
pagePerformance.description: Pages the tests measured: the Core Web Vitals the browser recorded, and Lighthouse scores, against each step’s limits. — means this browser does not measure it.

smsInbox.title: SMS inbox
smsInbox.description: Codes sent by text message, for Wait for SMS steps. Set the inbound address below as the incoming-message webhook of your test numbers at Twilio, Vonage or any provider that posts To and Body (or to and text). Messages are kept seven days.
smsInbox.copyNow: Inbound address — copy it now, it will not be shown again
smsInbox.none: No inbound address: no message can arrive.

emailDelivery.title: Email delivery
emailDelivery.description: Invitations, password resets and run notifications include HTML and plain text. SMTP acceptance does not confirm delivery.
emailDelivery.error: Email delivery history could not be loaded.
emailDelivery.notConfigured: Email sending is not configured for this organization.
emailDelivery.noTracking: Delivery and bounce tracking is not configured.

dashboards.saveFailed: Could not save. If another member changed this dashboard, reload before trying again.
dashboards.name: Dashboard name
dashboards.editorDescription: Add up to 20 widget instances. Shared dashboards use each reader’s project permissions.
dashboards.projectUnavailable: Project unavailable. You do not have access to this widget’s project.

emailProvider.title: Organization email
